analysis: Examined ProviderLoop.swift base 1024-1290 (ModelSlot, signer selection, unchanged) and head 1-533. The PR adds `operatorModelFilter: Set<String>?` (head 221-224) and initializes it in init (head ~946-948) as nil when backend.enabledModels is empty, otherwise enabledModels ∪ config.models IDs. This is local operator policy (the operator is the adversary ADV-001 in TB-003 anyway). It affects which coordinator-pushed models are served and A-018 availability only. It touches no crypto, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011/T-052..T-057), cache scoping (T-041) or the add-on hold (TB-012). Nil means 'serve anything the coordinator pushes', which matches the stated prior behavior when enabled_models is empty, so it does not widen an operator restriction. The union with config.models means start-selected models stay allowed even if they are absent from enabled_models. This looks intentional and is not a security regression, since coordinator routing and attestation remain authoritative. Integration questions remain for other batches. (1) Where `operatorFilterAllows` is applied: prefetch/desired-models reconcile, applyVerifiedPrefetch, autopilot downloads and load_model. Check that a filter miss fails closed and does not bypass the weight-hash or self-test gates (failedSelfTestHashes, retiringModels). (2) Whether live model switches update the filter consistently with ordinaryServingModelIDs. These callers were not supplied, so no finding is made.
